implementation_notes: Rust's default realisation: the table and its columns are declared once in a schema module with the table! macro and the entity is a plain struct deriving Queryable/Selectable with #[diesel(table_name = ...)]; the macros expand the mapping into types, so there is no runtime reflection and no persistence code in the struct. Choose it when compile-time-checked queries matter; SeaORM's DeriveEntityModel is the async, entity-centric alternative, and sqlx keeps the mapping fully explicit with no metadata at all.
pitfalls: The schema module is a declaration separate from the struct: a column rename must be applied to both sides, and the CLI regenerates only one of them.
#[derive(Queryable)] binds by column order unless the select list is explicit, so adding a column can map values into the wrong fields.
Mapped structs own their data; borrowed row types live only as long as the connection/lifetimes allow, which constrains how far entities can travel.

variants.name: SeaORM DeriveEntityModel entities
variants.implementation_notes: SeaORM's variant: the entity struct derives DeriveEntityModel and the macro generates the Entity, Column and PrimaryKey companions from it, so the struct stays a plain data holder while the generated companions carry the metadata. Choose it for async services that want an entity-centric ORM without maintaining a separate schema file.
pitfalls: Derive attributes are the mapping: renaming a field without updating column_name changes the SQL silently.
Generated Entity/Column types exist alongside the struct; keep domain code on Model and let only the persistence layer touch the companions.
